Raza — thank you for the opportunity to put this together. Everything in it comes from one MLS® pull run in mid-October: every detached sale of 3,000 sq ft or more within 1.5 kilometres of your door since June 1, and every one currently for sale. The sections on value come first, the listing plan follows. One thing shapes the whole document: the buyers for a home like yours are active through November and thin out quickly once December and the holiday season arrive, so the timing matters as much as the number. Our reading of the evidence is stated once, at the end, and labelled as ours.

Section 01 · The property

A 4,766 sq ft custom residence, completed in 2019, on a 62-foot lot off Denlow Boulevard.

35 Longwood Drive South is a detached two-storey built in 2019 in the Banbury-Don Mills community, south of York Mills between Leslie and Banbury, with park views from the upper floor. The home has 4,766 sq ft above grade: five bedrooms, each with its own ensuite, two powder rooms, a main-floor office and a walk-through pantry, with a finished walk-out lower level that adds a sixth bedroom and ensuite, a second kitchen, a gym, a sauna and heated floors throughout. Stone and stucco exterior, a heated driveway, automatic blinds, three fireplaces and a built-in double garage complete it.

Sales are down 9% on a year ago and prices 5%, but sold-to-list is unchanged at 98%: homes priced to the market still sell near asking, it simply takes a deeper pool of buyers to get there — and that pool is thinnest at the top. Detached sales over $2M are down 21% on September 2025 and 10% year to date, and Toronto's $3M+ detached market has run at 37–58 sales a month since July against 66–76 in the spring.

Board statistics stop at the district line, so we pull our own MLS® data — every detached sale and active listing within 1.5 km of your door — and refresh it on the 1st of each month, before the board publishes on the 7th or 8th. Section 05 is that pull. You will receive it every month we work together, so a shift shows up in time to act on it.

Section 04 · Comparable sales since June 1

Four sales of 5,000 sq ft or more within 1.5 km. Nothing between 4,000 and 5,000 sq ft sold.

The MLS® search covered detached two-storeys of 3,000 sq ft or more within 1.5 km, closed on or after June 1: ten sales. Six of them were 1960s–70s homes of 3,200–3,500 sq ft, or a lot sold with building permits — a different buyer, and set aside here (Section 05 shows them as the pocket's floor). Four remain, and every one is larger than your home. That is the shape of this market: a 4,766 sq ft home sits between the original stock and the estates, and the value has to be read from the larger homes downward.

Section 05 · What the pocket did

Two markets within 1.5 km: under $2.5M sells in days at asking; above $4M has taken about three months at 90% of list.

SYNERGY's own pull — every detached sale of 3,000 sq ft or more within 1.5 km since June 1 — shows one pattern: the time it takes to sell rises with the price. Under $2.5M, original 1960s–70s homes went in two to nineteen days at or above asking. Above $4M, the three sales took six weeks to five months and closed at 81–95% of asking. Your home is in the second group, where the calendar matters most.

Section 06 · What each sale tells us

One close comparable, one ceiling, and two that show what size alone does not buy — ranked by what the photographs show.

10 Penwood Cres · Bayview & York Mills

$4,450,000

Sold September 18 · 144 days · 81% of list

The closest comparable in size and price. A 5,001 sq ft home of 1970s architecture backing onto Windfields Park with a concrete pool, on a 73-foot lot; 4+1 bedrooms and five bathrooms. The photographs show a clean, bright renovation — light oak floors, a white kitchen, new bathrooms — inside the original shell: compact rooms, standard ceiling heights, a galley-scale kitchen. It has more of almost everything your home has outside — frontage, a pool, parkland, the Bayview side — and less of what yours has inside. Listed at $5,499,000 in April and sold in September for $1,049,000 less. Two lessons: this is what a 5,000 sq ft home with every outdoor advantage cleared at this autumn, and this is what opening 23% high cost in time.

17 Sagewood Dr · Bayview & York Mills

$4,520,000

Sold September 15 · 41 days · 95% of list

The ceiling. A 6,000 sq ft custom Georgian by architect Tom Spragge on a 92 × 140 lot, with a four-car garage, circular drive, cedar-shake roof and pool. Immaculate and traditional: a panelled library, a red formal dining room, a cream kitchen with granite, carpeted bedrooms — a 1990s house kept beautifully, not a modern one. Listed at $4,750,000, close to its value, and sold in six weeks at 95%. A home 1,200 sq ft larger than yours on a lot 30 feet wider, in the most expensive part of the community, made $4,520,000. Your value sits below this on size and lot, and above it on finish.

29 Junewood Cres · St. Andrew-Windfields

$5,382,500

Sold August 19 · 84 days · 93% of list

The top of the local market this year, and the only sale finished to the standard of your home or above it. A new limestone estate of 6,140 sq ft above grade — nearly 9,000 in all — with coffered ceilings, a glass-railed staircase, a home theatre, a wine cellar, an elevator, a heated three-car garage and a pool, on a lot widening to 90 feet. Not a like-for-like comparable; it is here to show what another 1,400 sq ft and estate-level specification buy, which is roughly $1,000,000 over your range — and to show that the one modern house in the set is the one that sold highest.

19 Vernham Ave · St. Andrew-Windfields

$3,500,000

Sold June 6 · 44 days · 88% of list

The most instructive sale for your home. A 5,239 sq ft owner-built contemporary from the 1980s with an 80-foot frontage, a pool and 4+1 bedrooms — larger than yours in every dimension — listed at $3,998,000 and sold for $3,500,000. The photographs explain the price: original kitchen, glass-block bathrooms, carpet, pastel tile. It closed $950,000 below Penwood on size and lot that were, if anything, better. Buyers at this level are paying for how a home was built and when, not only for how big it is. That is the whole case for a 2019 build.

The pattern

Ranked by what the photographs show, the four sales run Junewood (new, estate finish — $5,382,500), Penwood (renovated inside a 1970s shell — $4,450,000), Sagewood (immaculate, traditional 1990s — $4,520,000) and Vernham (1980s original — $3,500,000). Size did not set the order: Vernham, the second-largest, sold lowest, and Sagewood needed 6,000 sq ft and a 92-foot lot to edge past Penwood. Three of the four were priced within 5–7% of where they sold and closed in six to twelve weeks; the one that opened 23% high took five months. At 4,766 sq ft, built in 2019, 35 Longwood is the smallest of the five and, with Junewood, one of only two finished as a modern house. The evidence places it alongside Penwood and below Sagewood on size, above both on finish — which is the top half of the range.

The two Bayview-side sales bracket your home from above on size and land: Penwood at $4,450,000 with more lot, a pool and parkland but a renovated 1970s house, and Sagewood at $4,520,000 with 1,200 sq ft more on a lot 30 feet wider but a traditional 1990s interior. On finish, your home is closer to Junewood than to either of them, and that is worth real money at this level — enough to put 35 Longwood at parity with Penwood at the top of the range. The smaller lot, the absence of a pool and the Leslie side of the community set the bottom. Vernham at $3,500,000 is the reminder that size without newness does not carry the price; your home has both.

This estimate is built from the records and the photographs on file. A walkthrough — the finishes, the lower level, how the house sits on the lot and against the park — is what turns it into the number we would put on a listing agreement.

Section 08 · Who you would be competing with

Twenty-one detached homes are for sale within 1.5 km. Nine are in your price bracket, and two of them are in your pocket.

A buyer looking at your home in November will have these open in other tabs. The seven Bridle Path and Windfields estates between $8.8M and $15.8M and a 100 × 563 ravine property are left out; what remains is the field you would be judged against — and five of the nine have been on the market more than 100 days. The two that matter most are in your own pocket: 20 Blaine at $4,490,000 after 193 days and 27 Hurlingham, brand new, at $5,290,000 after 167. Nothing in the set has cleared above them.

20 Blaine Drive

$4,490,000

193 days · 5,232 sq ft (MPAC) · built 1990, renovated 2022 · 62 × 140 corner · no pool · Lawrence & Leslie

The listing that defines your price point. Same side of the community, the same 62-foot frontage on a deeper corner lot, 466 sq ft more than yours, renovated top to bottom in 2022 with seven full bathrooms. It opened at $4,998,000 in the spring, came down to $4,490,000, and has not sold in six months. It is a renovated 1990 house, not a 2019 build, so it is not a measure of your value — but it is a clear demonstration that buyers here are patient, and that $4.5M is a number they are prepared to wait out.

Section 09 · Two ways to price it

Two ways to price it — and why the number is not final until we have walked through.

The range in Section 07 and the list prices below are an educated estimate, built from the records, the MLS® data and the photographs on file. We have not yet been inside. The walkthrough — the finishes, the lower level, how the house sits on the lot and against the park — is what turns the estimate into a pricing strategy we would put our name to, and it can move the number in either direction.

Both columns assume a launch within a week of the walkthrough, with photography, video and the ad campaign ready on day one.

Questions sellers ask

The things most people want to ask, answered before you have to.

Why not list higher and come down if we have to?

Because at this price the market reads the days. 10 Penwood opened at $5,499,000 and sold five months later at $4,450,000. 20 Blaine opened at $4,998,000 in the spring and is still for sale at $4,490,000. The buyers for a $4M+ home in this pocket are few, they know every listing, and the first fortnight is the most attention your home will ever get. The step-down option in Section 09 is there if you want to test the top — with the step agreed before we launch, not after.

What if it hasn't sold by December?

Then we will have two to three weeks of showing and traffic data and a clear read on why. We agree in advance what a slow first fortnight means. The point of launching in mid-November is that the question gets answered while the buyers are still active, not after they have gone quiet for the holidays.

Does a home like this need staging?

Yes — and it is already done. The home shows as a staged home today, and staging is covered in the Concierge package offered for this file, so there is nothing for you to arrange or pay for. What we add is the editing: which rooms are photographed and how, the lower level shown as the suite it is, and video that moves through the house the way a buyer would.

How long does it actually take?

About three days of preparation from the signed listing to live on MLS®, then a firm sale typically in four to six weeks at this price. Closing is usually 60 to 90 days after that, and the date is negotiable to suit your plans.

Do I pay anything if we don't sell?

No. Commission is earned on a completed sale. Staging, painting, photography and video at the Concierge level are ours to carry.

What happens to my taxes?

If 35 Longwood has been your principal residence for every year you have owned it, the gain is generally exempt and the sale is tax-free. Confirm the details with your tax advisor before closing; if you have questions, ask Terrence directly.

Who will I actually be dealing with?

Terrence leads the file. Behind him is a five-agent team and in-house legal review. You are never waiting on one person's calendar, and nothing sits because someone is away.

What if I change my mind?

Tell us. We would rather pause a listing than push a family into a sale they aren't ready for. We've built this business on families who came back and who sent their relatives.
